principles: One dominant scroll idea per scene; secondary recipes should be lower salience.
Do not combine two high-salience scrubbed camera/object motions on the same progress range without a clear hierarchy.
Pinned sections must earn their scroll distance with new information or spatial progression.
Typography motion must never make essential copy unreadable.
Mobile can choose a different recipe family from desktop.
goodPairs: Low-salience depth can support restrained type reveals.
Persistent object state changes are a natural fit for chapter-based pins.
Camera focus can support spatial annotations when movement pauses during reading.
Environmental drift can make section handoffs feel continuous.
Media crop and restrained line masks can share one editorial rhythm.
Lateral traversal works for maps/timelines when the content structure is inherently sequential.
avoidPairs: Two simultaneous navigation metaphors can disorient the user.
Nested or consecutive long pins create scroll jail unless exceptionally justified.
Multiple high-salience type effects compete with reading hierarchy.
Heavy 3D transforms plus video/frame scrubbing often exceed the performance and attention budget.
Stacking grain, particles, fog, color drift and light drift creates motion noise.
